about: Chris Doran's calibration feedback, run 1 (14 Nov 2026), exported from the calibration page's database. Verbatim, typos included. Fault verdicts: agree = fault and severity right; sev = fault right, severity in note; no = not a fault. C06–C10 were marked without fault-by-fault verdicts. stages = Chris's rating of each later stage for the chart as uploaded.

C01.leadNote: Lead is far too wordy. It describes facts, not drawing a conclusion. Should be punch first, qualifiiction/detail after
C01.ownLead: Man City had the fastest growing commercial revenue in the League
C01.issues: Need to include performance in the league. Need to adjust for inflation by indexing relative to average. Put labels next to lines, eliminate legend. Simplify axis to 08/09 format. Include CAGR calculation when you are talking about growth, humans cannot eyeball a line and determine CAGR%
C01.answer: Most important are no conclusion and no league performance. All others less critical

C02.ownLead: Man Citys commercial revenue ran far ahead of its football record from 09/10 to 17/18
C02.issues: You are talking about a relationship between two variables. Always try an X-Y plot whenever you have this. Put these axes together, mapping time from point to point.

C03.leadNote: Simplify - should be a sentence, with most important part first, then details and qualifications
C03.ownLead: Transit-stations are driving attractive growth for K&C with 9% CAGR
C03.issues:
1) Change lead to make relevant to client
2) Tidy up chart - eliminate axis, gridlines and legend, put format left of corresponding 2023 chunk, round revenue to HK$m, put unit in title, add total revenue, add CAGR % for each format on right; consider adding ranked bars on right hand side with ranked CAGR by format

C03-2.note: Hard to get a full action so what from just this data

C03-3.note: hard stop - false conclusion - delivery kitchens are fastest growing

C04.leadNote: A terrible conclusion, without logic that reinforces our clients prejudice
C04.issues:
Cannot draw conclusion from just this data; needs more analysis
Put all detailed numbers of each business in a table in the appendix for Q&A reference
Always seek a better chart than a pie chart
C04.answer: Always do logic. Until logic fixed, no point giving feedback on the cosmetics "No point putting lipstick on a pig"

C05.leadNote: Store profit variability is just "padding" or "motherhood" - what you say when you have no conclusion. Reanalyse the data to find the pattern. Equally, rents rising too fast - for what?
C05.issues: Never presenta table like this to your client. At best, it is an appendix page, for reference in Q&A. It is lazy cut and paste from Excel. There is no visual focus to follow the lead, it will take a client 5 minutes to figure everything out
C05.answer: No, push the whole chart back and redo lead - what do they want to say?

C06.leadNote: Focus on the decision - which to fund first. Also the maths is not right, the EBIT is lifted to $90m
C06.issues:
Highlight pricing programme
Add sources
Add units
Typos - Procurement
C06.answer: Yes - typos and numbers wrong in the lead are hard stops, major everywhere else

C07.ownLead: Push price rises in 2026 to recover margin
C07.issues:
The lead and so what are about margin, but this is not on the chart. Include it - as a separate line with data labels rounded to 10
Show CAGRs on time series charts
C07.answer: One primary fault. No point repeating the main fault with small variations in language

C08.leadNote:
Terrible lead - not enough data to support this conclusion
Look at the data - is there a strong correlation between sales and spend?
C08.ownLead: Marketing spend has a weak correlation with sales
C08.issues:
Our lead is about the relationship between marketing spend and sales. Try XY plot for a relationship, like the Man City chart. Impossible for humans to eyeball a chart and see if there is or isnt a relationship
Dual axis charts usually are not the best choice
C08.answer: Causal claim demolished first. They should relook at the data and write a new lead on weak correlation. Then draw a new chart for the new lead. Then Danial can critique the chart

C09.leadNote: Enter vietnam first is the so what conclusion we are building towards - it is not enough data to support it yet. Simplify the lead
C09.ownLead: Vietnam is the fastest growing room A/C market in ASEAN, at 9.8% CAGR
C09.issues:
anNual growth typo is obvious
% a year label not needed. Instead put unit - $ or units, CAGR% and time under the ROOM A/C DEMAND title
ChartGPT source is a hard stop
C09.answer: As my feedback - not enough on its own. suggest adding more data - eg profitability to support conclusion on market attractiveness, combine with competitive position to get GE matrix entry conclusion

C10.leadNote:
Cant support conclusion on "most " yet. 
Dont use numbers where they are artificial
C10.ownLead: Kestral should fully invest in Elderly care as our most attractive business
C10.issues:
Bubble area = $xm revenue should be a legend, not in title.
Source  - doesnt come from management accounts.
GE Matrix always has market attractiveness vertical - changing it will confuse people
Mark the dotted lines
C10.answer: Good choice of framework for the decision
